device.description: quadruple 8-bit voltage-output DAC with serial interface (DATA, CLK, LOAD), LDAC and per-DAC x1/x2 range bit

registers.name: INA
registers.note: DACA input latch (double buffered, Table 2); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: INB
registers.note: DACB input latch (double buffered, Table 2); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: INC
registers.note: DACC input latch (double buffered, Table 2); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: IND
registers.note: DACD input latch (double buffered, Table 2); power-on value not given (0 used)

registers.name: RNG
registers.note: per-DAC range bits (0 = 1 x REF, 1 = 2 x REF) from the serial word, collected in one internal register

commands.name: Write DACA
commands.note: A1 A0, RNG, D7-D0 MSB first (Figure 1, Table 2)

commands.name: Write DACB
commands.note: A1 A0, RNG, D7-D0 MSB first (Figure 1, Table 2)

commands.name: Write DACC
commands.note: A1 A0, RNG, D7-D0 MSB first (Figure 1, Table 2)

commands.name: Write DACD
commands.note: A1 A0, RNG, D7-D0 MSB first (Figure 1, Table 2)

protocol.note: with LOAD high, DATA is clocked in on each CLK falling edge (CLK low between bytes, Figures 3-4 -> mode 1); LOAD pulsed low transfers the last 11 bits (address, RNG, D7-D0) to the selected DAC input latch: LOAD is an active-high frame pin and the command is decoded from the last 11 bits before LOAD falls (16-clock two-byte transfers with leading don't-care bits, Figures 3-4)

ldac.note: LDAC low: the selected DAC output updates when LOAD falls; LDAC high: the value is held until LDAC is pulsed low (p.3)

device.note: tlv5620.pdf (SLAS110B) p.1 (D/N pinout, description), p.2 (terminal functions), p.3 (data interface, Table 2 serial input decode), p.4 (Figures 1-2), p.5 (Figures 3-4), p.7 (recommended operating conditions: VDD 2.7-5.25 V, timing)

notModeled: analog: voltage outputs, reference inputs; the RNG bit (x1 / x2 range) is stored only
power-on contents of the latches are not given (the datasheet only says a power-on reset gives repeatable start-up conditions; 0 used)
a LOAD pulse after fewer than 11 CLK bits: the model ignores it (the datasheet does not define it)
serial timing requirements (recommended operating conditions table)
